records.legislative_authority_finding: Special Law of 12 January 1989 article 68(1) expressly gives the Assemblée réunie and Collège réuni joint ordinance-making authority and gives the members initiative. The earlier COCOM organisation page contained unrelated casino material; its claims are corroborated using independent parliamentary publications and law. It is not the sole authority.

records.name: Nunatsiavut Assembly
records.decision: Add the Nunatsiavut Assembly as a regional autonomous special-status legislature under the Labrador Inuit treaty/constitution. Provincial nesting does not remove its regional legislative status.
records.legislative_authority_finding: The treaty establishes legislative and executive institutions and grants lawmaking in substantive fields, including education and health (chapter 17, parts 17.12 and 17.13). Labrador Inuit Constitution 4.18.1 vests that treaty-defined lawmaking competence in the Assembly; 4.18.2 requires Assembly passage and presidential assent. This establishes a regional legislature, beyond collective ownership or consultation.
records.budget_and_executive_control_finding: Constitution 4.1.3 assigns lawmaking and government oversight. Sections 3.2.7–3.2.8 require the First Minister to retain Assembly confidence; 8.8.3 requires Assembly approval of the annual consolidated financial plan. Assembly Act 51–53 provides witness/document powers with jurisdictional and judicial/independent-body exceptions.
scope_limits: This is not a fourth Canadian territory or a province. Retain the autonomous Inuit government relationship within Newfoundland and Labrador.
Treaty lawmaking has subject, territorial and personal limits; federal/provincial conflict rules differ by field. Do not describe it as unlimited sovereignty.
Local Inuit Community Councils remain a separate local-government class; the regional Assembly decision does not automatically include them.
The legal decision does not certify current membership, every constitutional amendment, or media availability.

primary_evidence.instrument: Labrador Inuit Land Claims Agreement, official federal publication
primary_evidence.finding: Treaty-protected self-government requires legislative/executive institutions and provides actual education/health lawmaking; competence and conflict rules are specifically delimited.
primary_evidence.currentness: Official federal treaty text read on 24 October 2026. This finding concerns the established legislative framework, not a legal opinion on every later amendment.

primary_evidence.instrument: Labrador Inuit Constitution, Schedule A to Nunatsiavut Constitution Act

primary_evidence.currentness: Original enacted 1 December 2005 source; core authority corroborated by treaty and maintained current legislation index. Not a fresh consolidated membership/seat-count certification.

records.name: Sámi Parliament of Finland
records.decision: Retain in the excluded/boundary ledger as an Indigenous cultural self-government and representative body. Its current enacted powers do not establish an autonomous territorial legislature under the project rule.
records.legislative_authority_finding: Act 974/1995 as amended by Act 414/2025 sections1,5–6 establishes cultural/linguistic self-government, own decisions in that remit, representation, initiatives and proposals. Sections9–9 b strengthen negotiation/cooperation aimed at agreement or consent for state measures affecting Sámi rights. They do not confer a general power to enact substantive territorial laws.
records.budget_and_executive_control_finding: Sections2,8 and13–15 provide state financing, autonomous use of operating funds and cultural grants, and an internal board implementing plenary decisions. These are real self-government powers, but managing institutional grants/operations and participating in state decisions does not satisfy the territorial lawmaking and territorial executive-control gate.
scope_limits: This is a scope decision, not a denial of Sámi constitutional status or self-determination.
The new cooperation and negotiation duties must not be reduced to a casual consultation label. The current reform and aim of obtaining consent are expressly retained.
Do not apply the result to Åland or automatically to Sámi institutions in other countries.

Act 414/2025 commencement/transitional provisions leave pending pre-commencement section 9 matters under the former rules and preserve the sitting term; do not infer an immediate new election/composition in 2025.

records.name: Holy Community of Mount Athos
records.decision: Resolve the original candidate as the wrong organ for the legislative inventory: Holy Community is the regular administrative body. Retain a cross-reference to the distinct extraordinary twenty-member Synaxis as the qualifying autonomous legislative organ.
records.legislative_authority_finding: Constitution 105(2) assigns administration to the Holy Community. Charter 43 identifies the extraordinary twenty-member Synaxis as the highest legislative/judicial organ and expressly excludes the regular representatives from that legislative body. The original Community name must not absorb the Synaxis lawmaking powers.
records.budget_and_executive_control_finding: Charter 35 makes the Community approve the common-fund budget and additional expenses and inspect executive accounts; Holy Epistasia executes. Administrative finance control alone does not make this particular organ the legislature.
scope_limits: Mount Athos remains a constitutionally self-governed part of Greece; Greek sovereignty and state public-order supervision are preserved.
Do not classify every monastery council, spiritual tribunal or the Holy Epistasia as a legislature.
The identity correction does not exclude all Mount Athos territorial lawmaking; the corrected Synaxis is recorded separately below.

The Charter/decree text is published by a constituent monastery. It is not a current consolidated state-gazette certificate; current constitutional article105 independently confirms the governing framework.

related_inventory_correction.name: Extraordinary Twenty-Member Synaxis of Mount Athos / Έκτακτη Εικοσαμελής Σύναξη
related_inventory_correction.decision: Retain the corrected organ as eligible autonomous special-status territorial lawmaking; do not treat it as an ordinary municipality or as a second jurisdiction.
related_inventory_correction.legal_basis: Charter 43 names the legislative organ; ratifying decree 6 empowers it to enact regulations consistent with the Charter, subject to ministerial confirmation (Patriarchal approval for purely spiritual provisions). Charter 36 grants determination of compulsory common-fund contributions; decree 33 provides for setting court expenses/fees by Synaxis regulation.
related_inventory_correction.scope_reasoning: The constitutional territorial regime and binding non-spiritual rules/compulsory territorial institutional revenue clear the autonomous special-status bar. Spiritual/monastic status alone neither establishes nor defeats eligibility. Finance/executive administration is divided among the Synaxis, Community and Epistasia; record their distinct roles.
related_inventory_correction.currentness_limit: Foundational law was read from a constituent institution; no claim that every 1926 provision remains wholly unamended. Current Constitution 105 and independent government description corroborate organ separation.

counting_note: The corrected Athos Synaxis replaces a misidentified legislative-organ candidate; it is not a second Mount Athos jurisdiction. COCOM is a distinct formation sharing Brussels regional membership.

additional_regional_inventory_records.legislative_authority_finding: Governance Agreement2.1–2.3 establishes local/regional arrangements;4.8 defines regional territorial reach;8.12 gives environmental/natural-resource/pollution lawmaking and8.15 direct taxation. Constitution11.1–11.3 places enactment/publication in the regional council. These operative regional treaty powers establish more than a coordinating service board.
additional_regional_inventory_records.budget_and_executive_control_finding: Quebec Act respecting the Cree Nation Government(G-1.031)46–49 assigns executive powers through council bylaws/appointments;81–83 requires annual council budget adoption and accessible accounts. Constitution11 establishes a public regional lawmaking procedure.
scope_limits: CategoryIA and related treaty land scope is specifically delimited; this is not a legislature with blanket jurisdiction throughout all of Quebec or all of Eeyou Istchee.

Agreement8.8 expressly conditions exercise of marriage/matrimonial-property/language-culture powers8.2,8.3 and8.6 on implementation agreements with Quebec. Those instruments have not been independently established here; eligibility relies on the separate operative regional powers8.12/8.15, not an assumption that all conditional powers are active.
The provincial municipal powers held in other legal capacities do not determine this treaty-law capacity.
Local Cree First Nation councils remain excluded by the requested individual-community tier boundary; do not duplicate them as regional legislatures.
